title: How Pipe Sizing Affects Your Home's Water Pressure
description: Undersized pipes are one of the most common causes of annoying water pressure drops in homes. When multiple fixtures run at once, a main line that is too small simply cannot supply enough volume, forcing water velocity too high and restricting flow. Maintaining a proper three-quarter-inch trunk line before stepping down to half-inch branch lines ensures adequate volume reaches your fixtures simultaneously. Proper pipe sizing also prevents noisy water hammer and reduces internal pipe wear from excessive friction. If running the laundry causes your shower pressure to plunge, your piping layout may need a professional sizing evaluation.
